task: DAEO-2gc7 (W2-68) batch 1 of 3 — first fold the lead's amendment E into the design note, then build the two fingerprints, the row each store load records, the incremental record load, the store-freshness check and `python3 -m gov.close.batch refresh`.

work_completed: (1) Amendment E is in the design note: §11 has a new point E; §3 drops the `FINGERPRINT_UNKNOWN` refusal and gains steps 8–10 (the batch commits its run record, closes each ticket in-process one after another, stops at the first refused close, then gives the envelope); §4 condition 4 now says a record naming no JUnit XML is never reused; §6's `run` row and §9's residuals (the queue keeps its own gates; the batch runs no gitleaks scan) match. The note was committed alone. (2) `gov.close.fingerprint.of_commit(root, commit)` gives `{"code", "records"}` as `sha256:` hashes of the sorted `ls-tree -r -z --full-tree` lines, all read from git objects of that commit. `record_only` comes from the commit's own test map, judged by the schema in point B's order. The path map, the test map and both schema paths always count as code. It returns None when the fingerprints cannot be computed (no map, a map that does not parse or fails its schema, no schema, an unreadable commit). It reads git through `repo.git`. (3) `gov.store.load` writes a one-row `fingerprints` table (head, code, records, kind `rebuild`). That table is kept out of `_TABLES` and out of `_digest`, so `gov.rebuild.check` is unchanged. (4) `gov.store.load_records` raises `STORE_CODE_CHANGED` (exit 1) when there is no store, no row, no code fingerprint, or a different one. Otherwise it reloads every graph table from HEAD (`commit_paths` included), calls `lexical.refresh` and `semantic.refresh` as `gov rebuild` does, leaves the code index alone, and writes the kind `records`. It fails closed: the row's records fingerprint stays empty until the indexes are refreshed, so a load that breaks halfway leaves the store stale. It also refuses if HEAD moves to other code during the load. (5) `repo.store_is_of_head` keeps today's rule, then: when a row exists, its head is HEAD and both fingerprints equal HEAD's; when HEAD's fingerprints cannot be computed, the row must be a `rebuild` of HEAD; a store with no table is judged by today's rule alone; a table without exactly one row counts as stale. (6) `gov.close.batch` has its command-line frame and `refresh` only: the API-0002 envelope as `nightly.main` gives it, exit 0 when the store is fresh at HEAD, else exit 1 with the error's code (`STORE_CODE_CHANGED`, or `STORE_STALE`).

(2) Every close's `_check_store` now computes HEAD's fingerprints (about 0.15 s here). (3) The fingerprint joins its sorted lines with a trailing newline each. If a later acceptance case recomputes the fingerprint its own way rather than comparing two of them, that byte format would decide it. (4) `gov rebuild` writes the row before it refreshes the lexical index (the existing order). A rebuild that fails at the lexical step leaves a row that says fresh — as fresh as today's commits rule would judge it.
lessons: Use the launch sandbox's TMPDIR, not `/tmp/gov-os-lead-W2-68`. Fixtures need `shared_core` with at least one pattern. Put the load<20 wait inside the background command itself.
